patch.value: Branch merge is an unrecorded mutation: the field-aware merge produces an item state that no history entry ever produced, so the merged state is unaddressable by restore and point-in-time reads

The field-aware merge driver converges item files correctly but writes no history entry for the resolution it computed, so the surviving item state has no address in the append-only record.

Live reproduction on 2026.7.25 in a throwaway git repository with pm merge install applied:

  base commit: item created, then updated (stream length 2)
  branch agent-a: comment_add, update (status in_progress), note_add   -> stream length 5
  branch agent-b: comment_add, update (priority 1), learnings_add      -> stream length 5
  git merge agent-a into agent-b

Convergence is good and should be recorded as such: zero conflict markers under .agents/pm, the stream unions to 8 entries with no cross-author loss, the merged item keeps status in_progress from A and priority 1 from B, and all annotations from both branches survive. Point-in-time addressing of pre-divergence versions is stable: pm get --at 2 returns the same state before and after the merge.

The integrity hole is the merged state itself:

  pm history <id> --verify -> ok false, verify_failed:current_item_hash_mismatch,
      latest_after_hash f0dfb167..., current_item_hash 917a2941..., current_matches_latest false
  pm validate            -> validate_history_drift_hash_mismatches:1, history_drift warn, ok true
  pm history-repair <id> --dry-run -> chain_drift_before false, entries_rehashed 0

Repair correctly declines: the chain itself verifies end to end. The mismatch is between the last recorded after_hash and the hash of the item file on disk, because the merged field set was produced by the merge driver rather than by any recorded operation. No history entry describes it, no version addresses it, and pm restore cannot reproduce it. Every branch merge therefore leaves a permanent drift warning that no shipped command can clear, and pm validate reports ok true while carrying it.

This contradicts the append-only invariant directly: the merge is a mutation of tracked data, and the outcome milestone pm-w7ccmv requires restore-to-any-version and point-in-time reads to hold across merge. pm-76dnfg asserts a verifying chain after reanchor as a conformance property; this item owns the write-side primitive that property needs, namely recording the resolution as an entry whose patch is the merge outcome and whose provenance names the branches, drivers, and inputs it reconciled. pm-2sbj8p consumes it as evidence for the convergence model.

The merge resolution is recorded as a history entry whose patch reproduces the merged item state exactly, so the last after_hash equals the hash of the merged item file and pm history --verify passes with no manual step; The entry carries merge provenance: the contributing stream heads or branch identities, the driver that produced the resolution, and per-field attribution for any field where the branches disagreed; pm restore and pm get --at can address the merged state like any other version, asserted by a test that merges divergent branches and then restores to the post-merge version from the stream alone; A clean merge leaves pm validate with zero history-drift warnings, and a genuine tamper still fails, so the drift signal keeps its meaning; history-repair keeps declining to rewrite a verifying chain: recording the resolution is the fix, and repair is not extended to fabricate entries; Recording is deterministic and order-independent, so merging the same branch set in different orders yields the same merged state and equivalent recorded provenance; The workspace-scope equivalent is covered or explicitly deferred with a reason: settings, schema, and relationship artifacts merged by the same fence get the same treatment

Immediately afterwards pm history <id> --verify returns ok:false with errors [verify_failed:current_item_hash_mismatch], latest_after_hash f6b6065e... against current_item_hash a1c9cbfb..., and pm validate --check-history-drift reports drifted_items_count 1 with hash_mismatches 1. message: Link the entry-level ordering gap that sits underneath merge provenance

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Post-merge drift reproduced on the shipped 2026.7.26 build, 2026-07-26, isolated sandbox.

Two branches mutated the same item (A: comment + priority; B: comment + tag). git merge auto-merged both artifacts and the merge driver's own output reported reanchored: true, then immediately emitted guidance to run pm validate --check-history-drift and pm history-repair --all. pm validate directly after the merge reported validate_history_drift_hash_mismatches:1. pm history-repair --all then returned repaired: 1, skipped_clean: 0, failed: 0, and validate came back clean.

Two things worth separating on this item.

The driver reports a reanchor it has not finished. reanchored: true and a hash mismatch one command later are contradictory as read by an agent: the operation announced success, and the very next verification says the chain is wrong. Whatever the internal distinction is between re-anchoring the stream and reconciling the item hash, the merge output does not carry it, so the honest state after a merge is unrepresented.

The remedy is a manual second step on a path that is otherwise fully automatic. A merge that resolves cleanly at the git level leaves the tracker in a state that fails its own validation until a human or an agent remembers to run a separate repair. Every branch merge in a multi-agent workflow hits this, and nothing in the git flow forces the second command.

Note the contrast with the behaviour recorded on this item earlier: there, history-repair correctly declined with entries_rehashed: 0 because the merged field set had no entry to anchor to. Here repair succeeded. Both outcomes leave the same user-visible signature — a green merge followed by a red validate — which is an argument for the fix being in what the merge records rather than in what repair can recover.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Follow-on finding 2026-07-31, filed as pm-aka8m7. No reopen proposed: this item's resolution - receipt-backed merge_reconcile events making merged state replay-addressable - is delivered and holds.

The adjacent property it does not cover is provenance of the merge inputs. reanchorHistoryEntries overwrites each entry's before_hash and after_hash in place at src/core/history/replay.ts:365-370 and retains the prior pair nowhere. So after a union merge the merged chain verifies internally while no verifier can confirm that a given entry was written against the state its author observed, because the anchor the author committed to has been replaced by one computed from the merged ordering. Addressability of the result and verifiability of the inputs are separate guarantees, and pm-w7ccmv promises both.
